# Best travel chargers with multiple USB-C ports

**Best overall: UGREEN Nexode 100W (3× USB-C + 1× USB-A).** Two of the reviews I found pick it as their top choice. [TechWise](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) says either of its first two USB-C ports can deliver the full 100W alone. With a laptop and a second USB-C device it splits 65W/30W, and with all four ports in use it splits 45W/30W/10.5W. The downsides are that it's the heaviest of that review's three picks (8.3 oz) and it doesn't include a cable.
- Buy/price links: [TechWise review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) or [Android Central's charger guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/best-usb-c-phone-charger)
- One source, [VoyageHacks](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/), describes it as four USB-C ports. The other sources list three USB-C plus one USB-A, so check the listing before buying.

**Best compact: Anker Prime 67W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A).** It weighs 4.78 oz, and either USB-C port can output the full 67W alone. Output is about 65W with two devices and 64.5W with three. It supports PPS for Samsung and Pixel phones. It suits a laptop, phone and one accessory, but not a laptop and tablet together.
- [TechWise review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-gan-usb-c-chargers-travel-2026) | [VoyageHacks review](https://voyagehacks.com/en/travel-gear/best-gan-wall-chargers-for-travel/)

**Best for a power-hungry laptop: Anker 737 GaNPrime 120W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A).** It gives the most headroom for one demanding laptop, but power is still shared once other devices are plugged in.
- [TechWise review](https://www.techwisereviews.com/posts/best-usb-c-chargers-travel-multiple-devices-2026)

**Budget option: Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A), $49.99 for a 2-pack.** It delivers 65W from either USB-C port alone. With two or three devices connected, the laptop port drops to 45W, which is fine for a MacBook Air but slow for a 65W laptop. It has foldable prongs.
- [Buy at Baseus via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) (affiliate link, no discount code worked when tested). Dealectric said it had no Anker or UGREEN products in its records, so it wasn't comparing against them.

## Before you buy
- **Plug adapter:** These are US wall chargers with foldable prongs, so for international trips you'll need a plug adapter, not a voltage converter. If you'd rather have one device with swappable plugs, [Android Central's travel adapter guide](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/best-usb-adapter-for-travel) lists the Epicka TA-105 Max (75W, 3× USB-C, 2× USB-A) and the UGREEN 65W Nexode travel adapter (2× USB-C + 1× USB-A). The Baseus EnerCore CG11 from the same guide has only one USB-C port.
- **Cables:** Use a 5A e-marked USB-C cable for anything above 60W, or it will limit the charger.
- **Power sharing:** The headline wattage is the maximum, not what each port gets when several are in use. Plug your laptop into the highest-power USB-C port first.

If you tell me what you're charging (laptop model, phone, tablet) and whether the trip is domestic or international, I can narrow this to one pick.
